newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Unisource sees revenue growth without Telefonica.
newsitem.headline: Unisource sees revenue growth without Telefonica.

text.p: Unisource NV, the Netherlands based international telecommunications joint venture, said on Monday it expected strong revenue growth this year, even after Telefonica has left the group.

The Unisource partners of Koninklijke PTT Nederland, Swiss Telecom PTT and Telia of Sweden are teamed up with AT&T Corp in a business communications venture called AT&T Unisource, which Telefonica was asked to leave last Friday.
"In spite of the fact that we now lose some Spanish business, we will...be able to show a substantial amount of growth," Unisource chairman Lars Berg told reporters.

The partners asked Telefonica, part of the Unisource group since 1996, to leave after news on Friday it had forged an "incompatible" link with Concert, a rival alliance between British Telecom Plc and MCI Communications Corp.
Unisource, set up in 1992, reported a 1995 net loss of 320 million guilders, up from 41 million in 1994 but Berg said losses were being curbed.

"We firmly believe that we reached the lowest point when it comes to our loss-making last year. We have a clear tendency of very strong revenue growth this year that should also result in a better bottom line financial result," he said.
Unisource is planning to publish 1996 results in June. Earlier this year it announced 1996 turnover rose to 2.4 billion guilders, nearly doubling 1995's 1.32 billion guilders.
"Even without Telefonica we will be able to show a strong improvement in the loss situation this year. We're aiming for a break-even before the year 2000," said Berg.

Bob Aquilina, president of AT&T Europe, Middle East and Africa, reiterated AT&T's committment to the Unisource alliance. "Whatever others may suggest our commitment is unwavering, our confidence is unshaken," he told the news conference.
Aquilina added AT&T was well placed to expand in Latin America without the Telefonica link, despite analysts' views that Concert had stolen a march by hooking up with Telefonica.

"For Latin America it's important to know what we already have in terms of coverage. We have Alestra, which is in Mexico. We've spent more than $400 million in Mexico. We have operations in Puerto Rico, in Colombia and Venezuela, we are bidding on PCS (personal communications services) licences in Brazil," he said.
"To start with we have very good coverage into Latin America. We will continue to look at opportunities to expand that coverage as they come up," he added.
